SSD.note: Document states nothing on AI harms rules.
The only AI tool is a clinical decision system in health facilities, which belongs to the sectoral study.

facts.fact: WHO's South Sudan knowledge series (September 2026) reports the Digital Care Companion, a clinical decision support system on symbolic AI, logging 3,168 patient visits across 12 facilities in 10 States and Administrative Areas, with clinicians accepting its diagnosis recommendations.
WHO reports 64.9% of the Digital Care Companion's diagnosis recommendations were accepted by clinicians and 95.0% of 3,168 logged consultations were completed through all nine steps.

systems.platform: offline-first thin client with Starlink and solar

SSD.note: Document does not say the Digital Care Companion was built in South Sudan or by whom.
No rural connectivity programme or rural and urban internet use figures stated; Starlink is only a facility link.

facts.fact: The Digital Care Companion captures the full patient encounter digitally in the facility, building structured digital profiles that link visits, per WHO's September 2026 series.
WHO says the Digital Care Companion is logging visits at 12 facilities in 10 States and Administrative Areas and calls for phased expansion to more remote primary clinics.
WHO's September 2026 series states South Sudan's routine health reporting completeness is approximately 63% and timeliness approximately 52%.

SSD.note: Document names no national standards body or national IT standard.
Starlink is used as a facility link; no licence or sale to households or businesses is stated.
